questions.stem:
Statement: "Please do not safely lean out of the rapidly running train." - A public notice in a railway compartment.
Assumptions:
I. People usually deliberately ignore such printed public notices.
II. Leaning out of a rapidly running train is dangerous.

options.option_text: Only assumption I is clearly implicit
Only assumption II is clearly implicit
Both assumptions I and II are implicit
Neither assumption I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: A notice is always put up with the assumption that people will read and heed it, so assumption I is not implicit. A warning is issued because the act is dangerous, making assumption II completely implicit.

questions.stem:
Statement: "Use our brand new mosquito repellent to finally get a deep, good night's sleep." - A commercial advertisement.
Assumptions:
I. Normal people actually desire to get a good night's sleep.
II. Mosquitoes frequently cause a severe disturbance in sleep.

options.option_text: Only assumption I is clearly implicit
Only assumption II is clearly implicit
Both assumptions I and II are implicit
Neither assumption I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: Advertisements appeal to the desires of the public, so I is implicit. The advertisement directly links getting a good night's sleep to using mosquito repellent, assuming that mosquitoes disturb sleep. So II is also implicit.

questions.stem:
Statement: In a desperate attempt to severely reduce city air pollution, the local government has decisively decided to forcefully restrict the number of private vehicles driving on the road.
Assumptions:
I. Private vehicles are a major and significant source of city air pollution.
II. The general public will completely and blindly follow the government's strict restriction.

options.option_text: Only assumption II is clearly implicit
Both assumptions I and II are implicit
Neither assumption I nor II is implicit
Only assumption I is clearly implicit

questions.explanation: The government's action specifically targets private vehicles to reduce pollution, assuming they are a major cause (I is implicit). However, assuming the public will 'blindly' follow is an extreme assumption not supported by the statement. (II is not implicit).

questions.stem:
Statement: "Buy an incredibly expensive premium gym membership with us today to lose your excess weight fast!" - A fitness center's heavy promotion.
Assumptions:
I. People are generally actively looking to rapidly lose their excess weight.
II. A premium gym membership is the absolute only possible way to rapidly lose weight.

options.option_text: Only assumption I is clearly implicit
Only assumption II is clearly implicit
Both assumptions I and II are implicit
Neither assumption I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: A business promotes a product assuming there is a demand for the result (losing weight), so I is implicit. However, the promotion does not assume it is the 'absolute only' way to lose weight; it just promotes its own method. Words like 'only' usually make an assumption invalid.

questions.stem:
Statement: The rigid school administration has strictly completely banned the personal use of mobile phones inside the entire campus for all students.
Assumptions:
I. Personal mobile phones actively cause severe distraction in the educational learning environment.
II. High school students very frequently brought their mobile phones to school.

options.option_text: Only assumption I is clearly implicit
Only assumption II is clearly implicit
Both assumptions I and II are implicit
Neither assumption I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: A ban on an item in a school is enacted because it is considered detrimental to the environment (I is implicit). Furthermore, a ban is only necessary if the action was actually happening, meaning students were bringing phones (II is implicit).

questions.stem:
Statement: "If you urgently want to significantly heavily increase the daily sales of your new product, you absolutely must advertise it heavily on prime-time television." - A marketing expert's firm advice.
Assumptions:
I. Television advertising during the evening prime-time successfully reaches a truly massive consumer audience.
II. Literally no other alternative form of advertising can possibly increase the sales of the product.

options.option_text: Only assumption II is clearly implicit
Only assumption I is clearly implicit
Both assumptions I and II are implicit
Neither assumption I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: The expert recommends prime-time TV to increase sales, which inherently assumes that prime-time TV reaches many people who might buy the product (I is implicit). However, 'No other form' is an extreme and absolute assumption not logically derived from a simple recommendation. (II is not implicit).

questions.stem:
Statement: The local city municipality has publicly announced a massive, mandatory 50% cut in daily water supply for the next 3 days to urgently repair the main supply pipeline.
Assumptions:
I. Citizens will likely store adequate clean water for their basic survival needs for the next 3 days.
II. The complex repair work of the main pipeline is highly urgent and simply cannot be delayed.

options.option_text: Only assumption I is clearly implicit
Only assumption II is clearly implicit
Neither assumption I nor II is implicit
Both assumptions I and II are implicit

questions.explanation: The municipality makes an advance announcement with the exact assumption that citizens will take heed and store water (I is implicit). A drastic measure like a 50% cut over 3 days implies the repairs are critical and immediate (II is implicit).
